title: Replace a worn conveyor roller
instruction: Replace the worn red roller: put it on the green mat and drop the new roller into its slots.
context: Gravity conveyors in warehouses and packing lines use drop-in rollers whose axle ends rest in open slots; a worn roller is lifted out and a new one dropped in with a hand at each end, so both axle ends go in level at once.
setup: Between the arms: a conveyor section of two grey steel side rails (17 x 2 x 8 cm each, their centres 30 cm apart, 28 cm between their inner faces, running away from the arms from 16 to 33 cm in front of the arm bases), each with open U-slots 22 mm wide and 25 mm deep in its top, 20 cm and 30 cm in front of the arm bases. Two hollow aluminium rollers rest in the slots, each 4.8 cm across and 26 cm long on 12 mm steel axle stubs (34.4 cm over the stubs, each stub 4.2 cm long), 0.4 kg: a grey one in the nearer slots and a red, worn one in the farther slots. 11 cm in front of the arm bases, a new grey roller rests in a spare stand: two short grey steel posts (5 x 2 x 8 cm each, in line with the rails) with the same U-slots. A green rubber mat (12 x 30 cm, 1 mm thick, its long side along the line between the arms) lies on the table, centred 40 cm in front of the arm bases, past the rails' ends.
scoring: 1.0 if the red roller lies on the green mat (its centre over the mat, at most 1.5 cm above lying on the table), the new roller rests in the red roller's slots (both axle stubs within the slots' 22 mm width and 6 mm of the slot bottoms), the grey roller is still in its own slots, and all three are still for 1 second. Otherwise 0.4 for the red roller on the mat plus 0.4 for the new roller in the red roller's slots; 0 if the grey roller is out of its slots.
reset_notes: Put the red roller back in the farther slots and the new roller back in the spare stand.
fidelity: All parts are rigid: the rollers are cylinders with cylinder axle stubs (they don't spin on bearings, but roll freely where they rest), and the rails and stand are fixed boxes. The axle stubs are round where real drop-in rollers often have hex ends. Nothing is deformable.
